comments.text_zh: 我想这里大多数人已经看过了，但我觉得 Bret Victor 的 Inventing on Principle 演讲[1]是我看过的最好的演讲之一。我时不时会重看一遍，帮助自己避免思维陷入窠臼。把开发软件当作职业时，太容易陷入一种模式：一遍又一遍地使用同样的工具和技术。看这个演讲激励我去探索开发和交付软件的其他方式。人们很容易认为软件开发总是必须涉及代码，而且只涉及代码。但看这个演讲激励我去尝试 Node Red 和 Unreal Blueprints 这类东西。这两种情况下通常仍然会涉及代码，但它们都提供了一种可视化连接组件的方式。我觉得能够这样把软件可视化很有帮助，这样我就能立即理解数据如何在应用中流动。[1] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I think most here have already seen it, but I find that Bret Victor's Inventing on Principle talk[1] is one of the best I've seen. I re-watch it every so often to help prevent my thinking from falling into a rut. When developing software as a career, it's so easy to just fall into a pattern where you use the same tools and techniques over and over again. Watching this talk this talk inspires me to investigate alternate approaches to developing and delivering software. It's easy to think of software development as something that always need to involve code, and nothing but code. But watching this talk inspires me to go and try things like Node Red and Unreal Blueprints. In both cases, code is usually still involved, but they both offer a visual way of connecting components. I find it helpful to be able to visualize software this way so I can immediate understand how data flows through the application. [1] [VIDEO]

comments.why_zh: 程序与其输出之间的紧密耦合。
comments.quote_zh: 这类似 Bret Victor 的一些想法
comments.text_zh: 不，他们解释说 LabVIEW 和其他可视化语言只是表示代码的不同方式。我认为，这里的关键想法是，程序的输出与程序本身之间有紧密得多的耦合。这类似 Bret Victor 的一些想法：[VIDEO] 我想把这种耦合思路融入我自己的可视化数据流语言（[LINK]）中，但还没决定如何实现。我的做法是自底向上设计这门语言，让简单程序可以被简单地画出来，同时有更高层的编程结构来简化更复杂的代码，从而避免你在 LabVIEW 中看到的那种复杂性问题（Deutsch limit）。
comments.text: No, they explain that LabVIEW and other visual languages are just different ways of representing the code. The idea here, I think, is that there's far greater coupling between the output of the program and the program itself. It's similar to some of Bret Victor's ideas: [VIDEO] I'd like to incorporate this coupling idea into my own visual dataflow language ( [LINK] ), but haven't yet decided how to implement it. My approach has been to design the language from the bottom-up, so that simple programs can be simply drawn, and there are higher level programming constructs which simplify more complex code, avoiding the complexity problem (the Deutsch limit) you've seen with LabVIEW.

comments.author: borplk
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What would your ideal programming language be like?
comments.text_zh: 我认为编程语言下一次带来游戏规则改变的演进，是超越纯文本。自编程诞生以来，我们基本的编程构建块本质上并没有改变。我们仍然把程序仅仅当作一堆文件和文件夹，用作家写言情小说时用的同一类工具来编辑（是啊是啊，“intellisense”说到底也没那么智能）。我们不会通过在文本编辑器里写 RGB 值来创作美丽的图像。我们也不该用它们来创建高度复杂的软件系统。我们需要基于模型的编辑环境，让我们拥有丰富得多的软件构建块。我们必须让软件不只是文件里的字符。软件的“源代码”不是一本书。它是一个系统的蓝图，这个系统附带着元数据和约束。它不能一直舒舒服服地以扁平纯文本结构存在，供人使用。如果你感兴趣，可以去翻我以前的评论，我之前写过更详细的吐槽。是的，我已经准备好迎接那种不可避免又司空见惯的回复：“不行，这不会奏效，我们以前试过了，而且永远永远都不值得再试”。另外相关：[LINK]（其实我有点意外地、间接地导致了那个 subreddit 的创建，起因是之前我在 HN 上的一次讨论）[LINK] [LINK] [LINK] [VIDEO]
comments.text: I think the next game-changing evolution in programming languages is moving beyond plaintext. Our basic building blocks of programming has not changed essentially since the beginning of programming. We still treat programs as nothing but a bunch of files and folders edited with the same tools that writers use to write romance novels (yeah yeah "intellisense" is not so intelli at the end of the day). We don't create beautiful images by writing RGB values in a text editor. We shouldn't be creating highly complex software systems with them either. We need model based editing environments that will allow us to have a much richer set of software building blocks. We have to allow software to be more than just characters in files. Software "source" is not a book. It's the blueprint for a system that has metadata and constraints attached to it. It can't comfortably and forever exist in a flat plaintext structure for human consumption. If you are interested go dig up my old comments I have written more elaborate rants about it before. And yes I'm ready for the inevitable and customary "NO IT AINT GON WORK WE TRIED BEFORE AND IT AINT WORTH TRYIN EVER EVER AGAIN" replies. I think a Bret Victor, "Inventing on Principal" style editor would be perfect, combined with some sort of scratch like Python IDE where each element is defined in terms of its reactive behaviors with other elements on a timeline. I didn't say easy, I said not too difficult. Order of magnitude difference. :) [VIDEO] With some [LINK]
